label: BL
reason: User input flows through escapeHtml() which sanitizes HTML entities, then to format() sink. While HTML escaping prevents classic XSS, format string attacks (%s,%n) could theoretically bypass HTML escaping since escapeHtml() targets HTML entities not format specifiers. Reviewers may disagree on whether this constitutes a real vulnerability.

evidence.note: param from request flows through escapeHtml() to format() sink; HTML escaping protects against script injection but not format string specifiers
